steps.say: the distributive property, with $-1$ as the factor
commutative and associative: reorder and regroup

1.1/O1>1.2/O4.point: Collecting like terms is itself the distributive property: $5x^{2}-2x^{2}=(5-2)x^{2}$.

steps.say: distribute the first factor over the second

1.1/O1>1.2/O5.point: FOIL is not a separate rule. It is the distributive property used twice.

steps.say: write each term with the common factor showing
the distributive property, read right to left

1.1/O1>1.3/O1.point: Factoring is distributing run backwards. Multiply out to check.

steps.say: add $-12$ to both sides — the additive inverse
multiply both sides by $\tfrac{1}{3}$ — the multiplicative inverse

1.1/O1>1.6/O1.point: Every step is a property of the real numbers applied to both sides. Without them the steps are moves to memorise.

1.1/O1>8.1/O2.point: Sets obey commutative, associative and distributive laws with the same shape as arithmetic.

steps.say: the exponent binds tighter than the minus

1.1/O3>1.2/O1.point: The order of operations is what decides which number is the base.

1.1/O3>1.6/O1.point: Solving undoes operations in the reverse of the order that built the expression.

steps.say: the radical groups what is under it
the bar groups: the whole numerator over the whole denominator

1.1/O3>1.7/O2.point: Three grouping symbols at once — parentheses, radical, fraction bar. This is where the formula usually goes wrong.

1.1/O3>2.1/O2.point: Checking a solution is evaluating an expression. Precedence decides the answer.

steps.say: both differences are grouped by the bar

1.1/O3>2.2/O1.point: The bar means the whole numerator over the whole denominator, not term by term.

1.1/O3>3.1/O2.point: Substituting without parentheses gives $-9-12=-21$, a different number.

steps.say: multiply, then add — inside the denominator

1.1/O3>4.2/O2.point: The denominator has to be finished before the division happens.

1.1/O3>4.3/O4.point: The bar groups. It is not $\ln(40\div 5)$.

steps.say: the exponent applies to the bracket, not to 1000

1.1/O3>5.1/O2.point: Raising 1000 to the power first is the usual error, and it is an order-of-operations error.

1.1/O3>5.2/O1.point: Subtract before dividing: the bar groups everything above it.

1.1/O3>8.1/O5.point: Parentheses fix the order for set operations exactly as they do for numbers.

1.1/O3>9.1/O3.point: Multiplication before addition is the whole structure of an expected value.

steps.say: the bar groups the whole sum

1.1/O3>10.2/O1.point: Dividing only the last term gives $4+7+9+3=23$, which is the same mistake as $\tfrac{3x+6}{3}=x+6$.

steps.say: subtract the mean, then square — parentheses before the exponent

1.1/O3>10.3/O1.point: Four levels of grouping, evaluated from the inside out. Nothing here is new beyond 1.1.
